# RAM vs. Storage

These are two different types of memory in a computer, often confused because both are measured in gigabytes (GB).

## RAM (Random Access Memory)

- **Purpose**: Temporary working memory for active tasks
- **Speed**: Very fast
- **Volatility**: Contents are erased when power is off
- **Analogy**: Your desk — where you spread out papers you're actively working on
- **Examples of use**: Running apps, browser tabs, open documents

## Storage (SSD/Hard Drive)

- **Purpose**: Long-term permanent storage of files
- **Speed**: Slower than RAM (though SSDs are quite fast)
- **Volatility**: Data persists even when powered off
- **Analogy**: A filing cabinet — where everything is kept for later
- **Examples of use**: Operating system, apps, photos, documents, videos

## How They Work Together

When you open a file or launch a program, the computer copies it from storage into RAM so it can work with it quickly. More RAM lets you juggle more tasks at once; more storage lets you keep more files saved.

**Quick example**: If your computer slows down with many browser tabs open, you likely need more **RAM**. If you get "disk full" errors when downloading files, you need more **storage**.
